I had treatment resistant depression for over a decade. I nicknamed it "Adult Onset Failure-to-Thrive" because it was never about external factors- I just viewed it as some internal failing. I spent years working towards changing everything possible that I didn't like about my life... and I succeeded, mostly. But even once my situation was ideal, I still felt the same inside.

I tried Ketamine for the first time about 6 months ago. I've tried to describe the experience and the best I can manage is that it felt like rebooting my brain. Like my mind was a computer that had been left on too long and was bogged down with viruses. The ketamine "turned off" my brain through disassociation and when I "came back" my brain felt like it had been cleaned and restored. Approx 45 minutes after I took it, I experienced my first moments not plagued by suicidal ideation in over ten years. The effect persisted and relieved the worst of my depression symptoms for days after. I took Ketamine another 4-5 times over the course of two months. Though it was never as powerful or dramatic an experience as the first time, each subsequent trip continued to "reset" my brain and provide relief.

It's now been about four months since my last trip. I've been able to get off antidepressants and no longer have compulsive suicidal thoughts. I'm doing better at work and in relationships and for the first time in my adult life, I look forward to the future. I've had the opportunity to take it since but turned it down because at this point I feel like I got what I needed from it.

TL;DR: Ketamine cured treatment resistant depression I had lived with for over a decade. It's therapeutic benefits should absolutely be studied. If you're interested in learning more, check out: ketamineadvocacynetwork.org
